chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAnbasah, who said:

I asked him about a man who does not know whether he has performed one rakʿah or three. He said: He builds his salat (prayer) upon one rakʿah, then recites in it Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, and performs the two sajdahs of forgetfulness.

So the proper way regarding this report as well is that we interpret it as applying to the nawāfil, because the prescribed sunnah in them is to build upon the lesser number, and that is not the case in the obligatory prayers.

key_terms.الْبِنَاءُ عَلَى الْأَقَلِّ: basing the prayer on the lesser number when in doubt
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness or doubt in prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat (prayer) being continued on the assumed count
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah recited in the rakʿah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person doubts whether he prayed one rakʿah or three in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling for one who doubts the number of rakʿahs performed in salat (prayer). The concluding clarification states that this narration is to be understood as referring to supererogatory prayers, in which one builds upon the lesser number, not the obligatory prayers.
